content: Screening for prediabetes or type 2 diabetes in children and adolescents should be initiated when they reach puberty or at the age of 10 years, whichever occurs earlier, provided they have risk factors. Risk factors include being overweight, defined as having a body mass index (BMI) at or above the 85th percentile for age and sex, or being obese, defined as having a BMI at or above the 95th percentile for age and sex. In addition to being overweight or obese, the presence of one or more additional risk factors warrants screening. If the results of the initial screening are within normal limits, the screening should be repeated at least once every three years. However, if the child’s BMI increases significantly, more frequent screening may be necessary.
